summary: POC scoping focused on defining acceptance criteria and integrating MosaicLedger's custom harness. Key decisions: blended workload (75% streaming, 25% non-streaming) for initial benchmarks, p95 latency target for 512-token gen = 275ms on dedicated pool, telemetry + traces required for token-level breakdown. Network/VPC window and sample logs requested. Expected POC kickoff mid-August with 4-week benchmark phase.
topics: benchmarks: p95 latency, throughput, token cost
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-08-05 15:30 UTC | Duration 55m | Recording start
Attendees: Claire (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Rajesh (CTO), Maya (ML), Tom (Platform), Leila (SRE), Speaker 6 (sometimes on mute)
Shared artifacts: drive: tinyurl.com/mosaic-harness, sheet: Mosaic - benchmark matrix (link), example logs: mosaic_sample_1k.csv

00:00 Claire: okay everyone, thanks for jumping on, I'm Claire from Redwood inference, I'm the AE on the account, um Diego who you've met is our solutions engineer, we'll run through high level goals then get into the harness stuff and acceptance criteria.
00:14 Rajesh: yeah thanks Claire, quick context - MosaicLedger is evaluating inference for our fraud-detection assistant, we need both streaming (token-by-token alerts) and batch retrains, latency and cost both matter. We have compliance constraints too, SOC2 + some residency but mostly VPC.
00:30 Diego: great, quick Q - when you say streaming alerts, do you mean server-side streaming where responses are chunked, or your client reassembles? And, uh, what's the average prompt size?
00:43 Maya: mostly server-side streaming, clients expect partial tokens for early scoring; prompt sizes are typically 120 to 450 tokens, but we do have some long context cases to 1k.
00:54 Tom: adding, our platform will call Redwood via private peering for the POC — we need the IPs and firewall rules up front.
01:05 Claire: noted. For the POC we normally define success criteria across latency, throughput and quality. Diego, can you talk about typical acceptance buckets?
01:15 Diego: sure — we propose p95 latency targets, throughput targets for steady-state, and correctness/quality checks against a reference prompt-set. For MosaicLedger I'd recommend p95 for 512-token generation under 275ms on a dedicated pool, and a throughput of X qps sustained — we'll size once we see your historical qps. Also telemetry and token-level timing is required for root-cause on tail latency.
01:40 Rajesh: 275ms p95 is tight; are you accounting for KV cache warm/cold?
01:46 Diego: yes, we break out cold-start and steady-state. Cold-start tail will be higher, acceptance should be measured after warmup or with a cold-start SLA separate. Also we'll use prefix/K-V cash (sic) in the harness to emulate warm caches.
02:00 Leila: we need audit logs retention and event-level tracing — how do you surface that?
02:06 Claire: Redwood Console exposes per-request traces and token-level cost breakdown, we can offload logs to our S3 bucket or ship via your SIEM. We'll share the security pack.
02:18 Maya: moving to harness — our engs have Python scripts that call an internal client, they expect streaming chunks over websockets for latency-critical paths and HTTP batch endpoints for nightly scoring. We want the harness to run both modes.
02:34 Diego: perfect, we usually provide an adapter pattern — a small shim that maps your client calls to the harness interface. We ask for a sample of your request/response pairs, and a small client script. Can you provide 1k rows of logs with timestamps and latencies?
02:50 Maya: yes can do, we'll scrub PII first. Expect an export by Monday.
02:55 Claire: note that sample logs should include distribution of prompt lengths and where streaming vs batch happen. Diego, what about load shape?
03:04 Diego: propose initial load shape: 10-minute ramp to steady state, 30 minutes sustained at target qps, then a 10-minute ramp down, run three iterations for each configuration (streaming enabled/disabled, quantized model vs full float). We'll capture p50/p95/p99, and token-cost per thousand.
03:26 Rajesh: on model variants, we want to test two quantization profiles — 8-bit and 4-bit — and see perf vs quality. Does Redwood support both on dedicated?
03:34 Diego: yes, runtime can run both; 4-bit may change latency slightly, so we'll include it. Also for fallback we can route to a cheaper variant under load.
03:43 Tom: network question — for peering, will we need to open specific ports or just egress IPs?
03:48 Diego: primary requirement is egress IPs and allowed ports (443), plus optional mutual TLS if you want. We'll document the peering steps in the SOW.
03:55 Claire: ok timeline check — if you can deliver logs Mon (Aug 10th local), we can prepare harness and propose a kickoff week of Aug 17th. POC runs 4 weeks of active benching and two weeks for QA/analysis. Does that align?
04:12 Rajesh: yes that fits our internal roadmap. One ask — can you include a throughput-to-cost model in the SOW? We need cost per 1M tokens across modes.
04:21 Claire: absolutely. We'll include a cost sensitivity table and breakouts for streaming vs non-streaming token accounting.
04:28 Maya: for harness integration specifics — our client uses chunked JSON with sequence IDs, we need the harness to replay those slices as-is. Is the adapter flexible?
04:36 Diego: yes, the adapter is a lightweight Python lib; we can support chunked JSON and preserve seq IDs. We'll give an example adapter and tests.
04:44 Speaker 6: (inaudible) question about evaluation metrics.
04:46 Diego: for quality we'll run automated evals on the reference set — correctness, hallucination rate, and latency-impacting regressions. We also recommend human-in-the-loop review for any model variant that fails automatic thresholds.
05:00 Rajesh: accepted thresholds — can we document pass/fail rules? e.g. p95 < 275ms AND hallucination < 1.5% AND throughput >= target qps?
05:12 Claire: yes we'll draft acceptance criteria with pass/fail gates. We'll also flag which gates are 'must have' vs 'nice-to-have'.
05:20 Tom: on telemetry — we need token-level timing and sampling of full traces for failed requests. Is there library instrumentation or do we push logs?
05:28 Diego: both — we can instrument the adapter to emit spans to your tracing backend (Jaeger/Datadog) or send structured logs. We'll share the telemetry schema.
05:38 Maya: sweet. One more — streaming fallback behavior: if the stream path degrades, do you have automatic switch to non-streaming?
05:45 Diego: yes we have smart routing policies — the platform can automatically fallback to a compatible model or non-streaming endpoint. For the POC we'll test a stream-switch scenario where we cut streaming mid-run and validate correctness and latency.
05:56 Rajesh: what's the expected artifact set at the end of POC?
06:00 Claire: delivery includes benchmark report, cost model, telemetry dashboards, and a recommended deployment profile (dedicated sizing + quantization). Also we provide the harness adapter we used.
06:10 Leila: will we get logs for audits? retention?
06:14 Claire: yes we can provide audit logs for the POC timeframe and a recommended retention policy for the longer term — we'll include SOC2 scope in the security pack.
06:23 Maya: any blockers we should be aware of?
06:27 Tom: network org needs exact IPs and peering windows; security needs SAML metadata if you plan to SSO into the console.
06:34 Claire: action items captured — we'll send SOW, security pack, and the adapter. Diego will share the harness README with the expected script shape.
06:41 Rajesh: ok sounds good. Final check on workload split — we proposed 75% streaming 25% non-streaming for initial benchmarks?
06:49 Diego: yes that matches what you described earlier. We can sweep multiples later but start there.
06:54 Claire: perfect, thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the notes and the doc set.
06:58 Meeting close.

Notes on transcription: occasional speaker mislabels; some product names transcribed (Redwood Dedicated -> Redwood Dedicatede) and K-V cache spoken as K-V cash.
